messages.text: Hrgovic: Itauma is 'amazing' but boxed like an 'amateur'

metadata.summary: Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”.
metadata.content: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 Filip Hrgovic secured one of the biggest shocks in boxing this year after stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2; Hrgovic becomes Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion By David Rivers Sunday 30 August 2026 11:02, UK Image: Filip Hrgovic lands a punch on Moses Itauma (left) during his win Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”. Hrgovic, 34, became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Itauma, 21, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows. But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds. metadata.summary: The US Open, of all the four slams, is notoriously the hardest to predict the winners of as it falls at a time of year when eight months into the season the players are more likely than not nursing aches and pains with their bodies battered from the grind of the tour.

It's also played on a surface where more players fancy their chances; many have love-hate relationships with clay and grass but hard courts are their bread and butter. Al Aasy, William Haggas' veteran nine-year-old, has racked up 12 career wins in a fantastic career stretching back to 2019. He continues to show his enthusiasm for the game, winning at Beverley in July and running a solid third at Goodwood so deserves to step up in class again. Arrow Eagle represents the soon-to-retire Jean-Claude Rouget and carries the privilege of being his last Group 1 winner, taking the Royal-Oak last year. He might find this easier after being slightly disappointing when weakening in the Prix Vicomtesse Vigier. Norris claimed his maiden title in 2025 to become McLaren's first world championship winner since Lewis Hamilton triumphed for them in 2008. Having emerged victorious in an intense season-long title battle with his team-mate Oscar Piastri, Norris has further enhanced his status within the Woking squad by clearly outperforming the Australian so far in 2026.
